name: Brown planthopper (BPH) / hopperburn
signs: Patches of plants turn orange-brown and dry out, often in circular patches (hopperburn)
Many small brown insects at the base of the plants, especially in dense clumps
Sooty mold or honeydew at the base of the plants
actions: Check the base of the plants for small brown insects, especially in dense clumps
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer and split applications into smaller doses
Keep the field from standing water for long periods, following local water-management advice
Protect natural predators like spiders and mirid bugs by avoiding unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays
callExpertIf: The damage is spreading fast across the field or plants are collapsing
